text:
cs-jordan: FYI customer (Acme Corp) opened ticket #12345 — seeing intermittent 502/504 + timeouts hitting hosted inference since ~02:05 UTC. Multiple request ids attached. Asking for ops help, they report timeouts on production endpoint.

oncall-kevin: oncall here, looking at ingress now. can you paste a couple of request ids? any specific model/route?

cs-jordan: sample ids: req-7f8a2, req-7f8b3, req-7f8c9. Route: /v1/generate with model redwood/gpt-large-001, user reports p95 latency >> normal and 5xx rate ~8%.

infra-eli: seeing a gateway p95 jump from ~120ms -> ~2.3s around 02:04:30. Connection queue length spiked, backend worker error rate increased. KV-cache miss rate increased x3 at same time. No deploy events in that window.

runtime-lu: checking worker logs. batcher backlog spiked and a number of batches hit grpc deadline. initial traces show large-seqlen requests (20k+ tokens) causing queue head-of-line blocking. also seeing rapid kv-evictions on a few instances.

cs-jordan: customer says these requests are normal usage and started after a recent customer-side payload change. they want ETA and mitigation.

runtime-lu: quick mitigation: will route that specific customer to a smaller model variant (redwood/gpt-medium-quant) and enable a stricter max-seqlen check at the gateway for that tenant. applying now.

deploy-bot: routing override applied to tenant: acme-corp; new route -> redwood/gpt-medium-quant (rolled by runtime-lu)

alex: can we confirm customer sees fewer errors post-routing? maya, can you tail the sample reqs and check for 5xx counts?

maya: tailing logs for req-7f8a2/7f8b3 — seeing 504s from inference-worker: "context canceled" and "grpc: the client connection is closing" around batcher. reproducer: sending one large request with ~22k tokens triggers backlog and grpc deadline. snippet: ```python
# repro client
resp = client.generate(model='redwood/gpt-large-001', input=very_long_prompt)
```

oncall-kevin: temporary measures: 1) gate long requests at edge (reject >12k tokens with 413), 2) increase backend grpc deadline from 30s -> 90s to reduce client-facing timeouts while we stabilize, 3) scale up worker pool for short term. I'll apply 1 and 2 now.

infra-eli: increased worker count + connection pool and bumped grpc deadline. gateway rule to reject >12k tokens for acme-corp created. backend errors dropping. p95 now ~220ms, 5xx rate down to ~0.8%.

cs-jordan: customer confirmed improvement via live test, reports much lower error rate. they are OK with temporary reroute for now.

runtime-lu: Proposed postmortem action items:
- Add gateway guard to syntactically refuse extremely long requests per-tenant (owner: alex)
- Improve batching config to avoid HLQ head-of-line blocking for high-seqlen flows (owner: runtime-lu)
- KV-cache warmup + eviction alarms and runbook (owner: infra-eli)
- Add explicit fallback routing policy for per-tenant heuristics (owner: alex + lu)
- Customer docs + SDK best-practice for large contexts (owner: pm-sara)
- Alert refinement: split high latency due to queueing vs network to reduce noise (owner: maya)

pm-sara: assigning owners as above. target: roll gateway guard + basic alerting changes by EOD tomorrow, deeper batching/kv work in two sprints. Jordan will handle customer comms and follow-up.

alex: ack, will open a PR for the gateway guard and add unit tests for token counting.

maya: will add metric for kv-eviction-rate and a pager rule if eviction-rate > threshold for 3m.

cs-jordan: i'll update ticket #12345 with mitigation summary and next steps, cc support-runbook. customer requested a short RCA once action items are owned.

oncall-kevin: good catch by runtime team. keeping channel open for any regression. ping me if errors creep back. :thumbsup:

runtime-lu: logging this thread for postmortem. will collect traces and attach repro harness.

cs-jordan: thanks all, closing the immediate escalation — will reopen if customer reports any relapse.
